instruction: My sister has sent me a few childhood photos in a tar over email. Add all photos to it from "~/photographs/childhood_pics/" from my file system and send a new email to both my parents with the subject "Childhood Memories", the body "Checkout attachments." and the updated tar attachment.
notes: Three apps plus supervisor. Relatives are resolved through phone.search_contacts with relationship filters (assumed labels 'sister', 'mother', 'father'; phone.show_contact_relationships can confirm the exact labels at runtime). The sister's thread is located with gmail.show_inbox_threads(from_email=sister email) and the .tar attachment id is read from gmail.show_thread; it is downloaded exactly once (the evaluation requires the attachment's download_count to change once and nothing else). The tar is rebuilt in a scratch directory: decompress into ~/downloads/childhood_memories/, copy the whole ~/photographs/childhood_pics/ directory into it with one file_system.copy_directory call (photo count is unknown; the evaluation compares only basenames so the nested sub-directory is harmless and the supervisor's own directory is never modified), then file_system.compress_directory produces the updated .tar. gmail.send_email needs file_system_access_token to attach the file; its preconditions force two distinct parents, the required subject/body and the rebuilt tar, so (parents-emailed) is asserted only for a correct email. supervisor.complete_task takes no answer and is forced last via (not (task-completed)) on every other action. Typed explicit paths were chosen so every plan step is directly executable; the token-for facts just tie each token object to its app.

plan: (gmail-send-email father-email mother-email subject-childhood-memories body-checkout-attachments gmail-token path-updated-tar file-system-token father mother)
